handDesc.handNote: The main verse text is written in brown ink. Layout, visible signs and annotations are transcribed without assigning historical hands from colour alone. Long s and ordinary letter allographs are represented by standard Latin characters.

origin.p: The source manifest dates this composite manuscript to the 11th and 12th centuries. The catalogue date is not a date for every intervention.

surrogates.p: Actual source pages 392, 393, 394, 395 were inspected at full resolution and in enlarged crops. Viewer page numbers are one-based indices into the manifest, not manuscript page labels. e-codices IIIF source manifest

projectDesc.p: All 106 extant verse positions were first-read directly from witness S images. Existing annotation rectangles are reproduced without modification. No reading is supplied from LL or another witness. Word spacing and couplet grouping are editorial. A different agent has independently reviewed every source verse and note.

correction.p: Visible letters are retained even where they differ from familiar readings. Tentative paleography is localized with unclear. Uninscribed initial space is represented with space, with the visible small guide initial retained separately. No regular verse indentation is inferred from even numbering; whole-page source inspection shows aligned initials apart from the inset opening couplet. Marginal annotations are not silently substituted into the verse. Ink colour alone does not establish an erased reading or historical hand.

normalization.p: u/v and e caudata follow visible source forms as far as practicable. Long s and ordinary letter allographs use standard characters. Combining macrons represent visible suspension/contraction bars schematically. Abbreviations are paired with defensible expansions in choice/abbr/expan; unexplained letters are not expanded merely to match a familiar edition. Special glyph approximations are declared in charDecl. Their form is typographic rather than a facsimile drawing.

punctuation.p: Visible stops are transcribed as schematic dots or colons. Modern punctuation is not supplied. Word spaces are editorial except where space explicitly records a significant physical separation.

segmentation.p: Every verse has a stable ID and a facs pointer to a rectangle on the correct manifest canvas. Annotation page values are interpreted through the manifest index. Physical page changes are pb elements within logical couplets where necessary. Source text beyond the poem is used to verify boundaries but not included as verse.

interpretation.p: Every note has been investigated by a different source reader. Resolved observations document supported readings; remaining local uncertainties record limits of the scan and abbreviation interpretation, without automatically becoming user tasks. No human scholarly approval is implied.

div.head: Source observations and documented uncertainties
div.note: All four full pages confirm aligned regular initials without alternate-line inset. A small a is visible at the left of uninscribed initial space; only the opening two lines are physically inset. The candidate represents that space without inventing an inscribed decorated letter.
The second line shares the reserved-initial inset. The barred dominam abbreviation, looped p in propero, and parū plus crossed p are visible and explicitly expanded.
Raised i on t and barred s with t support the tibi and sunt expansions. The ending quę has the source e caudata. No extra que or tibi letters are presented as written out.
The enlarged crop shows a final e in rudente. Removed the unnecessary unclear while preserving the barred cȳba abbreviation and its cymba expansion.
The c belongs to preceding N̄c, not to the following word. The next written word is ruis, corrected from first-pass creuis. Appositis nubibus and solutus remain source readings.

Separate enlarged inspection identifies initial S, followed by tamē and later standū. Replaced tentative Stabū and flauiū with S and explicit tamen/standum abbreviation choices. No i is silently supplied after initial S.
The source reads pennas danaeus heros; all three words and the initial Nunc contraction are confirmed.
Terribile, barred densū and cū, and the suspended cap form are visible. Retained the explicit densum/cum/caput expansions and source singular-looking Terribile.
The middle e of cerealia is readable in the enlarged source. Removed its unnecessary local unclear; no overwritten earlier reading is inferred.

The contracted form has e caudata, suspension strokes and a us-like ending. The exact distribution of omitted letters is not certain; the existing qualified eternus expansion remains a documented abbreviation uncertainty.
The compact m and raised mark remain difficult to distinguish precisely. Retained the unexpanded unclear abbreviation rather than claiming a fully written mihi; the source seruilę remains visible.
In melię bithinide pallidus esse is visible; spelling and editorial word division are retained.
The suspended Dict form and adjacent et glyph are clear. Dicitur remains a qualified conventional expansion, with the actual contracted source form preserved.
The names xante neera are legible. No extra vowel or h is added.
The compact place-name still permits more than one reading in its middle. Retained qualified arethausę without borrowing an expected name.
The dark spot overlaps the bs-region of obstruante. The local stained uncertainty is appropriate; no physical deletion or hand assignment follows from the spot.
Pethia and occuluisse are legible; the suspended fer form remains expanded fertur. Both source spelling and contraction are retained.

The compact form contains more strokes than qns, tentatively qinq followed by a suspension sign. Revised the schematic abbreviation to unclear qinqꝫ and added qualified quinque expansion. The exact abbreviated letter shapes remain uncertain.

Enlargement supports sint and the final reqrā contraction, corrected from licet and referā. The short barred word before sint appears n̄c and is tentatively expanded nunc; the compact forms remain qualified. Acheloe is retained.
The large internal gap after fuit before tanti is visible. Its explicit space is retained, without metrical indentation.
Both tantę and barred tā are visible before bene. Neither word is omitted.

The first group begins in before a name tentatively ebantę; corrected the mistaken initial m in mebantę and divided words editorially. Ebantę and metopide remain unclear because their compact letter sequences are not fully secure.

The word after te is the barred pretereo contraction, not the proposed proper name spergeo. Corrected the abbreviation to p̄tereo with explicit pretereo expansion. The following qui, crossed-p per and uolutꝰ are retained.
The argiu-ending has a darker a-like form and overlapping strokes. Retained local unclear within dark ink; the image does not establish recoverable earlier letters or correction direction.
The dark spot affects cui. Current cui remains qualified because the local surface obscures part of the letters.
Notata is readable on enlargement. Removed its unclear; source comis and the second phrase lauata genas are retained.

The first word after Illa is gemens, corrected from genitoris. The group after patruique appears nefas rather than iniustas and is revised but remains unclear. Final marta remains tentative; no familiar verse is substituted wholesale.

The baseline word after Hanc remains unreadable under the brown disturbed patch; the dark amnis beneath is visible. Retained the gap and below-line addition separately, without inventing an erased word or a historical hand.
The source nostras contraction and phrase teris anxia ripas remain visible. The candidate retains those forms without grammatical normalization.
Ab ideo laomedonte genus is the visible sequence. No name is normalized.
The barred cōrumpis source form is clear, while the precise conventional expansion remains qualified. The contraction is retained rather than presented as written out.

The barred short form after colent has a compact terminal sign whose pen form is not fully secure. Retained the schematic abbreviation and low-certainty omnes expansion; no assumed amnes reading is substituted.
The source has flumina n̄ra tenent. The abbreviation and phrase are retained exactly.
The initial N of Nec is darker/crowded, without secure evidence of an erased earlier reading. Precor and propago retain their abbreviations; romana is preserved.
The enlarged word after promissis reads uberiora, with b and the following eri sequence visible. Corrected first-pass altiora. The source abbreviation promissis remains unchanged.
The short barred tē after fugā remains unexpanded. The sign alone does not securely determine its intended completion.
Currentia and eripiente metu are legible. The middle short group appears uirēs rather than uitū, but its compact ending and bar remain uncertain; it is revised within unclear and left unexpanded.

A dark E is visible to the left of the ordinary initial position, where the baseline initial is disturbed and unreadable. Retained separate add and gap, with no reconstruction of a prior character or erasure mechanism.
The enlarged baseline reads mea tecta forent patrioqꝫ sepulchro. Corrected first-pass detecta sorte pateatqꝫ; retained the visible -que contraction and explicit patrioque expansion.
The final legi is tentatively visible beside brown and dark staining. Retained the localized unclear without asserting additional lost words.
The m with raised o supports conventional modo expansion, now explicit. Source uestales tedas, inuitor and abbreviated adustus remain unchanged.
The written adultā has a contraction bar. Added a qualified adultera expansion while preserving the actual abbreviation; the completion remains explicitly uncertain.
The ending of famosus is readable in the enlarged crop. Removed its unclear and retained the separate source words que natet.
The middle bi of turbidis is visible on enlarged inspection. Removed unnecessary unclear while preserving crossed-p perdita and the source ending aquis.
The suspended Dict form repeats verse 26. Retained the explicit qualified Dicitur expansion and source thori.
The source reads latis spatiosus in undis. No additional i or other normalized wording is supplied.
The barred alt form is clearly abbreviated; added a qualified altus expansion, preserving the contracted source. The ending remains editorially uncertain, not a written-out source word.
The opening contraction Nōm is visible. Its Nomen expansion remains explicitly qualified, without pretending all letters are written.
The pluuiamque and niuesque contractions and final solutos agree with the source. Retained.
The last word still has uncertain middle letter shapes and remains tentative curtis. Brumale pectore is visibly written and is not normalized.

The short barred form appears p̄mis, tentatively expanded premis. The following contracted word appears arētē, tentatively expanded arentem; revised the first-pass p̄nus/attritā while retaining local uncertainty around these compact shapes.
The et-like dark group and following barred u-like form remain uncertain. No expanded word can be established securely from these shapes; both remain explicitly qualified.
The marked opening Dānosis and final is ending are visible. The Damnosis expansion is retained without changing the source vowel.
The middle consonant in Fortitan still has an ambiguous crossed shape. Retained local uncertainty rather than silently normalizing to Forsitan.
The short barred t after ego remains unexpanded. Narrabam, fluminum and amores remain source readings, with their contractions retained.
Sic spectans, acheloon and inachon remain the source reading. The final amnem contraction is retained; no imported proper-name spelling is substituted.

The short word after nomen has one tall l and small preceding strokes, appearing nile rather than uelle. Revised it to unclear nile; the initial minims remain a documented uncertainty rather than a confident normalization.
Semper and hiemps are abbreviated; the opening reserved-initial area of 3.7 below confirms the end after106. All 106 actual positions are covered.
The short form between Ulterius and ripa is n̄ro, with a bar and an r-shaped middle letter. Corrected first-pass noto to the explicit nostro contraction; petenda die remains the source wording.
A suspension bar is visible over the contracted diu-sis group. Added a choice retaining diūsis with explicit diuersis expansion; the source text is not presented as written out.
The source proper name has an ascender after p, giving asophon. Added the visible h omitted in the first-pass asopon.
A visible contraction bar occurs over the short u-ra form. Added a choice for ūra expanded uestra, preserving its abbreviated status.
The source has a separate si before nobile, with an s-shaped initial and following i. Corrected first-pass ignobile to si nobile; source legitimum and flumen contractions remain.
The visible sequence after diuitias is pigra ministrat, with final a on pigra before the next word. Corrected the first-pass misdivision and reading piger administrat.
